title: DigitMoney — Loan Marketplace & CRM
description: A fintech platform that matches borrowers with personal and business loan offers from partner lenders, backed by a CRM the operations team runs every day. Customers check pre-approved offers through a step-by-step application; agents and managers work leads, follow-ups, campaigns and disbursements in the admin panel.
usp: One application, many lenders: each customer is routed to the partners whose rules they match, while microservices handle lender integrations, messaging, reporting and short tracking links behind the scenes.

stackUsage.React: The customer site: multi-step loan applications with OTP verification, offer checks and lender-specific journeys, plus the admin panel.
stackUsage.TypeScript: The admin panel: dashboards for agents and managers, lead management, lender rules, campaigns, disbursements, bulk SMS and IVR.
stackUsage.Redux Toolkit: Shared state for the application flow and the admin's leads, filters and dashboards.
stackUsage.Tailwind CSS: The admin UI, with TanStack tables for large lead lists and FullCalendar for follow-ups.
stackUsage.Node.js: A set of focused services: core (users, leads, files), loan, alliance (lender partner APIs), messaging and reporting.
stackUsage.Express: REST APIs for each service with JWT auth and Swagger docs, clustered across CPU cores with throng.
stackUsage.MongoDB: Leads, customers, applications, lender rules and campaign data via Mongoose.
stackUsage.RabbitMQ: Queues between services, so lender calls, messages and reports run in the background without slowing the customer.
stackUsage.AWS S3: Customer document uploads, virus-scanned with ClamAV before they're stored.
stackUsage.Fastify + Redis: A fast URL shortener for SMS and campaign links, with Redis caching and bot filtering for accurate click tracking.

title: Atmaling — Storefront & Admin Panel
description: A mobile-first shop for festival idol bookings, plus the dashboard the shop runs it from. Customers browse the catalogue, build a cart, share it on WhatsApp and book without paying online; the team confirms each booking from the admin panel.
usp: Built around how the shop really sells: no forced sign-up and no payment gateway. Carts are shared as images on WhatsApp, re-priced live when opened, and bookings move through a status flow that refuses illegal jumps.

stackUsage.Next.js: The storefront: mobile-first, SEO-friendly pages for categories, products, the cart and shared carts that open at /c/CODE.
stackUsage.React: Component UI for both apps, sharing the same patterns across the shop and the dashboard.
stackUsage.Vite: Builds the admin dashboard: bookings with a status flow, a demand report of what's sitting unbooked in carts, products, categories, customers and live shop settings.
stackUsage.Express: The core API, layered as routes → handlers → helpers → models, with helmet, rate limiting, cookie sessions and Swagger docs.
stackUsage.MongoDB: Catalogue, carts, bookings and users with Mongoose; an aggregation over live carts powers "4 people have this in their cart".
stackUsage.Firebase Auth: Only sends the phone OTP. The server verifies Firebase's token, then issues its own 30-day HttpOnly session, so no customer data lives in Firebase.
stackUsage.Zustand: Cart and UI state in the storefront and dashboard, including the guest cart that merges into the account cart on login.
stackUsage.Tailwind CSS: Shared theme tokens so the light storefront and dark dashboard come from one design system.
stackUsage.Turborepo: Monorepo that builds both apps and the API together, with shared packages for the response envelope, money helpers and config.
stackUsage.sharp: Resizes uploaded product photos before they're stored on S3-compatible storage.

title: BillOCR — Bill Scanning & Inventory
description: Upload a photo or PDF of a supplier bill and get a reviewed purchase record. An AI vision model reads the bill, the app matches suppliers and products, flags price changes, and updates stock, price history and GST reports.
usp: The clever part isn't the OCR, it's the reconciliation: it knows "S/F MARIE LITE 200" and "Sunfeast Marie Light 200gm" are the same product, and only asks you to review the rows it's unsure about.

stackUsage.Next.js: App Router for the screens (upload, line-by-line review, products, suppliers, reports) and API routes for bills, imports and reports, deployed as one app.
stackUsage.TypeScript: End-to-end types from the extraction schema through matching, pricing and reports.
stackUsage.Claude API: Vision extraction that reads bill photos and PDFs natively, including handwriting and messy tables, into structured JSON.
stackUsage.MongoDB: Products, name aliases, suppliers, bills, payments and price history; aggregations drive the stock, purchase, HSN and ITC reports.
stackUsage.Zod: One schema validates the model's structured output and every database write.
stackUsage.Tailwind CSS: Dense data tables and the review screen where uncertain rows are confirmed.
stackUsage.Cloudflare R2: Stores the original bill files through signed upload URLs, with a hand-written SigV4 signer instead of a heavy SDK.
stackUsage.JWT (jose): Signed session cookie for the single-user login, checked in middleware before any page or API loads.
stackUsage.Excel export: Imports the existing product catalogue and exports bills in the Hitech accounting format with a zero-dependency XLSX reader and writer.

title: Hay Day Trading
description: A browser-based image generator for Hay Day players. Build Buy/Sell sheets and ratio-based trade listings with live price maths, style them, and copy a polished image straight into Discord.
usp: Turns a messy trade post into a share-ready image in seconds: live price and ratio maths, reusable sheets, and everything saved in the browser with no sign-up.

stackUsage.JavaScript: All app logic in plain modules (items, settings, persistence, overlays): listings, multi-item trades, selection modes and price and ratio calculations, with no build step.
stackUsage.jQuery: DOM updates and event handling across the editor, sheet switcher and styling drawer.
stackUsage.CSS: Responsive layout with a fixed styling drawer on desktop and an overlay on mobile, plus gradient, palette and text-style controls for the generated image.
stackUsage.html-to-image: Renders the listing to a PNG and writes it straight to the clipboard, falling back to a saveable image if clipboard access fails.
stackUsage.fuzzysort: Fuzzy item autocomplete with custom abbreviations, so typing "bem" finds "BEM Set".
stackUsage.math.js: Safe evaluation of price expressions, totals and trade ratios like 60:89.
stackUsage.Service Worker: Caches product images and Hay Day Wiki responses so repeat visits load fast.
stackUsage.localStorage: Keeps sheets, trade rows, styling and preferences between visits, with JSON export and import for backups.
